params.body:
I shipped this yesterday activating its own forty sources. It should not, and a live check of the queries it would have added shows why.

**A third of our confirmed concept names are not research questions.** Asked of OpenAlex today: "multi platform gaming efficiency" returns 42,597 papers whose first result is drone-assisted disaster response, and "aesthetic identity curation" lands in cosmetic medicine. Ten of those a day would have entered the corpus every day carrying academic authority, tier a and trust 1.2.

**And no automatic test separates them.** Volume is useless, because the bad queries return MORE than the good ones. A stricter field search still lands on ride-pooling and diffusion models. Anchoring the query in "youth" silences the good ones too: "brainrot gaming vernacular" goes from eight relevant papers to none. A person reading forty lines tells them apart in a minute, and the index cannot.

So the job now does what every other hand on this desk does: it proposes. The queries are created inactive under the same `source-proposed-` prefix the scout uses, so they appear in the same place, and a person switches on the ones that name something real.

Three rules, each with a reason. It proposes a query ONCE and never again, in any state, because a hand that keeps re-offering what was turned down is not proposing but insisting. It never approves. And a query whose concept has faded is reported rather than switched off, because that row is collecting and the call is a person's.

Left as it was: it never touches the six hand-written queries.

Suite 674 green. The weekly line in `ops/crontab` stays, and is now safe to run unattended, which the merged version was not: next Monday it would have activated forty unreviewed sources on its own.
params.title: The academic queries are proposed, not decided
